entries.title: Psalms 47:1
segments:
All ye people; that is, as the original word means, all ye nations. Here, as often elsewhere in the Psalms, the gentile nations are called upon to rejoice in God, in anticipation of their reception, through faith, into the church. 
 
God is the joy of his people.  In him they glory as their righteousness, wisdom, and strength.

entries.title: Psalms 47:3
segments: Under us; under his covenant people.  The victories of ancient Israel over the surrounding heathen nations foreshadowed the spiritual subjection of the nations to the church through faith in Christ.

entries.title: Psalms 47:4
segments:
Our inheritance--the excellency of Jacob; designations of the goodly heritage which God conferred upon his ancient people. 
 
The condition of each individual is chosen for him by God, and with it he should be content, and thus by his conduct say, Not my will, but thine be done.

entries.title: Psalms 47:5
segments:
God is gone up; from the conquest of his enemies to heaven. 
 
  A shout--the sound of a trumpet; the signs of rejoicing.

entries.title: Psalms 47:6
segments: Those who from the heart offer praises to God, glorify him.  In this, the high and the low, the rich and the poor, persons of all descriptions may unite, and thus secure his approbation and blessing.

entries.title: Psalms 47:7
segments: All the earth; God is not a local deity, but a universal monarch.

entries.title: Psalms 47:8
segments:
God reigneth over the heathen; they will one day all be brought to acknowledge and adore him as their King. 
 
The prophets of the Old Testament foresaw and predicted the day when all heathen nations shall be brought to acknowledge and glorify God, and he shall be greatly exalted throughout the whole earth.

entries.title: Psalms 47:9
segments:
Gathered together; to worship God and acknowledge him as their Lord.  These are the princes of the heathen mentioned in the preceding verse. 
 
  The people of the God of Abraham; who had become such by their submission to him. 
 
  The shields of the earth; the same as the "princes of the people,"
